references.text: Moses appointed overseers over the people, mentioned in the same context as Joshua's later use of them.
Judges and overseers were appointed by Moses for all the tribes, the same administrative structure that Joshua now employs.
The overseers had the responsibility to speak to the people before war, the same role they have here as Joshua prepares for the entry into Canaan.
The overseers went through the camp and gave instructions to the people to follow the ark of the covenant, a direct fulfillment of Joshua's command.
Moses originally established overseers as leaders over the people on Jethro's advice.
The seventy elders and overseers were given by the Spirit of the Lord to help Moses lead the people.
